1: # Project: vigil-agent (Phase 1: Foundations & Architecture Scaffold)
2: 
3: ## Architecture
4: Vigil is an open-source, self-hostable proactive AI assistant and execution harness. Phase 1 establishes the rock-solid foundations and module-driven architecture scaffold:
5: - **FastAPI Backend (`backend/`)**: Modular architecture with dynamic router factories and ASGI middleware pipeline.
6: - **Strict Protocol Boundaries**: Every domain module defines persistence and external interaction solely through `@runtime_checkable typing.Protocol` abstractions in `repository.py`. Zero SQL, zero ORM, zero HTTP calls in `repository.py`.
7: - **Constructor Dependency Injection**: `service.py` implements all domain logic, accepting `session` and `settings` via constructor injection.
8: - **Factory Router Pattern**: Zero bare module-level global `APIRouter`s. Every module exposes `build_<module>_router(settings: Settings) -> APIRouter`.
9: - **Central Dependency Hub**: `backend/src/dependencies.py` re-exports all providers for one-stop injection.
10: - **Uniform Error Handling**: All errors inherit from `AppException` returning `{"code", "message", "request_id", "details"}` with correlation header `X-Request-ID`.
11: - **Security & Pairing**: SHA-256 token hashing, AES-256-GCM secret encryption, startup ASCII QR code pairing flow.
12: - **Containerized Deployment**: Multi-service Docker environment (`postgres` with pgvector, `api`, `worker`).
13: 
14: ## Feature Inventory
15: | # | Feature | Description | Milestone | Source |
16: |---|---------|-------------|-----------|--------|
17: | F01 | Monorepo Directory Scaffolding | Top-level folders: `connectors/gmail/`, `mobile/`, `web/`, `skills/`, `deploy/`, `docs/` | M1 | R1 |
18: | F02 | UV Python Environment | `backend/pyproject.toml` targeting Python >=3.12 with all core and test dependencies | M1 | R1 |
19: | F03 | Core Settings Configuration | Pydantic v2 `BaseSettings` loading DB, ports, secrets, tiered models, and LLM keys | M2 | R2 |
20: | F04 | Uniform Exception Hierarchy | `AppException` with `NotFoundError`, `UnauthorizedError`, `ForbiddenError`, `ConflictError`, `ValidationError` | M2 | R2 |
21: | F05 | Uniform Error Serialization | FastAPI exception handlers returning `{code, message, request_id, details}` echoing `X-Request-ID` | M2 | R2 |
22: | F06 | Structured Logging Pipeline | JSON/text logging with contextvars propagating `request_id` | M2 | R2 |
23: | F07 | Security & Crypto Primitives | SHA-256 `hash_token`, `verify_token` and AES-256-GCM `encrypt_secret`, `decrypt_secret` | M2 | R2 |
24: | F08 | Request ID Middleware | ASGI middleware extracting or generating UUID `X-Request-ID` header and contextvar | M2 | R2 |
25: | F09 | Timing Middleware | ASGI middleware measuring request processing latency in `X-Process-Time` | M2 | R2 |
26: | F10 | Idempotency Middleware | ASGI middleware enforcing `Idempotency-Key` validation on mutating requests | M2 | R2 |
27: | F11 | Root API Router Factory | `create_api_router(settings)` dynamically aggregating module routers under `/api/v1` | M2 | R2 |
28: | F12 | 14 Domain Module Skeletons | Scaffold modules (`health`, `auth`, `cards`, `triage`, `runs`, `approvals`, `chat`, `artifacts`, `memory`, `compaction`, `skills`, `connectors`, `settings`, `jobs`) | M3 | R3 |
29: | F13 | Pure Repository Protocols | Strict `@runtime_checkable typing.Protocol` abstractions in `repository.py` with 0 SQL/ORM | M3 | R3 |
30: | F14 | Module Services & DTOs | `service.py` constructor DI and `data.py` Pydantic DTOs for all 14 modules | M3 | R3 |
31: | F15 | Module Router Factories | `build_<module>_router(settings)` factory across all 14 modules | M3 | R3 |
32: | F16 | Central Dependencies Hub | `backend/src/dependencies.py` centrally re-exporting all providers | M3 | R3 |
33: | F17 | External Integration Protocols | `backend/src/integrations/repositories.py` abstracting Jev, LLM, Sandbox, MCP, Notifications | M3 | R3 |
34: | F18 | Working Health Module | `GET /api/v1/health` returning liveness and DB readiness probe | M4 | R4 |
35: | F19 | Device Pairing Flow | `POST /api/v1/auth/pair` validating pairing code and issuing long-lived bearer token | M4 | R4 |

53: ## Interface Contracts
54: 
55: ### Error Response Contract
56: All error responses from FastAPI endpoints must conform to:
57: ```json
58: {
59:   "code": "ERROR_CODE_STRING",
60:   "message": "Human-readable explanation",
61:   "request_id": "uuid-string",
62:   "details": null | {}
63: }
64: ```
65: Headers:
66: - `X-Request-ID`: echoed from request or newly generated UUID.
67: - `X-Process-Time`: execution latency formatted e.g. `0.001234s`.
68: 
69: ### Router Factory Contract
70: Every module router must be defined as:
71: ```python
72: def build_<module>_router(settings: Settings) -> APIRouter:
73:     router = APIRouter(prefix="/<module>", tags=["<module>"])
74:     ...
75:     return router
76: ```
77: No module may define a bare global `router = APIRouter()`.
78: 
79: ### Repository Protocol Contract
80: Every `src/modules/<module>/repository.py` must contain:
81: ```python
82: from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
83: 
84: @runtime_checkable
85: class <Module>Repository(Protocol):
86:     ...
87: ```
88: Zero imports of `sqlalchemy`, `sqlmodel`, `tortoise`, or raw SQL.
89: 
90: ### Security Contract
91: - `hash_token(token: str) -> str`: Returns SHA-256 hex digest.
92: - `verify_token(token: str, token_hash: str) -> bool`: Constant-time comparison.
93: - `encrypt_secret(plaintext: str, secret_key: str) -> str`: AES-256-GCM base64 encoded.
94: - `decrypt_secret(ciphertext: str, secret_key: str) -> str`: AES-256-GCM decrypt.
95: 
96: ### Auth & Health Wire Contracts
97: - `GET /api/v1/health` -> `200 OK` `{"status": "ok", "version": "0.1.0", "database": "connected" | "disabled"}`
98: - `POST /api/v1/auth/pair` with `{"pairing_code": "VIG-...", "device_name": "My Device"}` -> `200 OK` `{"device_token": "vgt_...", "device_id": "uuid", "device_name": "My Device"}`
99: - `GET /api/v1/auth/me` with `Authorization: Bearer vgt_...` -> `200 OK` `{"device_id": "uuid", "device_name": "My Device", "created_at": "...", "last_seen_at": "..."}`

47: ```
48: 
49: `APP_ENV` defaults to `development`. `deploy/docker-compose.yml` sets `APP_ENV: ${APP_ENV:-development}`.
50: So a stock deployment accepts any bearer token whose value starts with `vgt_test`.
51: 
52: **Proof, run against the real app factory:**
53: 
54: ```
55: vgt_testtoken             -> 200
56: vgt_test_anything_i_want  -> 200
57: vgt_prod_real_token       -> 401
58: ```
59: 
60: This is a wildcard bypass, not four seeded test values. The prefix check on line 228 admits the whole namespace.
61: 
62: **Fix.** Delete the branch. Seed test devices from a fixture in `tests/conftest.py` alone.
63: Guard the seeding class with `if self.settings.APP_ENV == "test"` and nothing else.
64: Add a regression test that asserts 401 for `vgt_test_anything` with `APP_ENV=development`.

66: ### P1-2. All authentication state lives in class level dictionaries
67: 
68: `AuthService._active_pairing_codes`, `_devices`, `_devices_by_id`, `_users` are `ClassVar` dicts.
69: 
70: Consequences:
71: 
72: 1. Every device token dies on restart. The user must re-pair after each deploy.
73: 2. The pairing code printed at boot dies on restart. The QR code in the log becomes stale.
74: 3. Two API replicas do not share state. A token issued by replica A fails on replica B.
75: 4. Nothing reaches the `devices` or `users` table defined in the specification.
76: 
77: This contradicts architectural tenet 2. Run state and identity state must be durable.

79: **Fix.** Implement `AuthRepository` against the `AsyncSession` that the service already receives. The service ignores its `session` argument today.
80: Phase 2 delivers the tables. Until then, keep the in-memory store behind a `DeviceStore` Protocol and mark it `development` only, so the production path cannot use it.

89: 200 {'status': 'degraded', 'database': 'error', ...}
90: ```

98: `Settings.SECRET_KEY` defaults to a constant 64 character hex string. `.env.example` repeats it.
99: `deploy/docker-compose.yml` passes `DATABASE_URL` and `APP_ENV` to the containers. It does not pass `SECRET_KEY`.

101: Result: every stock deployment encrypts connector credentials with a key that is published in the repository.
102: 
103: **Fix.**
104: 1. Add a validator. If `APP_ENV == "production"` and `SECRET_KEY` equals the default, raise at startup.
105: 2. Add `SECRET_KEY: ${SECRET_KEY:?SECRET_KEY is required}` to both services. The `:?` form fails the compose file when the value is missing.
106: 3. Add `env_file: ../deploy/.env` so the file is the single source.

109: 
110: Two problems in one loop.
111: 
112: **The reaper.** `reap_stale_locks(timeout_seconds=300)` runs every poll cycle against `locked_at`. The worker never updates `locked_at` after the claim.
113: Any job that runs longer than 5 minutes is reaped and claimed by a second worker. Two containers then write to the same workspace. This is defect B2 from the specification review, now in code.
114: 
115: **The dispatch.** `src/worker.py:50`
116: 
117: ```python
118: await asyncio.sleep(0.01)  # Simulate non-blocking task
119: await jobs_service.mark_completed(job.id)
120: ```
121: 
122: Every claimed job is marked completed, whatever its type. A `gmail_send` job reports success without sending. That is worse than a crash, because the audit trail records a delivery that never happened.
123: 
124: **Fix.**
125: 1. Add `heartbeat_at`. Update it every 30 seconds. Reap on `heartbeat_at` with a 90 second limit.
126: 2. Replace the sleep with a dispatch table. An unknown job type must fail with a clear error, never complete.
127: 3. Add the `priority` column now, while the table does not exist yet. Changing it later means a migration on live data.

28: 
29: ## 1. Executive Summary & System Philosophy
30: 
31: Vigil acts as an autonomous personal chief of staff. It continuously monitors incoming communication streams, tracked tasks, deadlines, and project milestones. Rather than passively waiting for user prompts, Vigil triages events using a cost-efficient decision model (Jev), surfaces actionable notification cards to a companion Flutter mobile app, and executes complex multi-step coding, document compilation, file transformation, and communication runs inside an isolated Linux sandbox under an approval-first security model.
32: 
33: ### Key Architectural Tenets
34: 
35: 1. **Approval-First Execution**: The agent can inspect files, write code, run compilers, and generate artifacts freely inside its isolated Docker sandbox. However, **any external side-effect** (sending an email, creating external drafts, publishing webhooks, modifying third-party accounts) strictly pauses execution and requires user approval via the mobile card UI.
36: 2. **Stateless Process Deallocation**: When an execution pauses for human approval or an asynchronous background task, the worker process **releases all memory and terminates**. Run state is serialized entirely within PostgreSQL. Approvals hours or days later resume execution seamlessly, surviving server restarts and container evictions.
37: 3. **Single Datastore Simplicity**: By running relational state, the atomic worker queue (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), and vector memory (`pgvector`) within PostgreSQL 16+, Vigil eliminates the operational complexity of Redis, Celery, or external vector databases for self-hosters.
38: 4. **Decoupled Connectors via Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: External services (Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub) are not hardcoded into core application logic. They are implemented as standalone MCP connectors that expose polling capabilities and tools governed by standard approval policies.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 2. Viability & Why Traditional Agent Architectures Fail
43: 
44: ### The In-Memory Trap
45: Most popular agent frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, naive Pydantic AI loops) maintain execution state in the runtime memory of an async Python thread or generator:
46: 
47: ```python
48: # NAIVE AGENT PATTERN (FAILS IN PRODUCTION)
49: async def run_loop():
50:     while not done:
51:         response = await model.call(history, tools)
52:         for tool_call in response.tool_calls:
53:             if tool_call.requires_approval:
54:                 user_ok = await wait_for_user_approval(tool_call) # BLOCKS IN-MEMORY!
55: ```
56: 
57: This pattern fails in production environments for four critical reasons:
58: 1. **Thread/Memory Exhaustion**: If a user takes 6 hours to respond to an approval notification, a worker thread or process remains locked in memory. At scale or on self-hosted VPS nodes, system resources are quickly exhausted.
59: 2. **Server Restart & Eviction Vulnerability**: If the server restarts, containers roll out, or a cold start occurs, all active, paused, or queued runs are dropped and lost.
60: 3. **Parallel Tool Call ID Desynchronization**: Modern LLMs (OpenAI GPT-4o, Anthropic Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5) frequently emit *multiple parallel tool calls* in a single turn. For example:
61:    $$\text{Turn } N \rightarrow [C_1: \text{read\_file}, \ C_2: \text{compile\_artifact}, \ C_3: \text{gmail\_send}]$$
62:    The model API requires that every single tool call ID emitted in Turn $N$ must receive a corresponding `role="tool"` message before Turn $N+1$ can be called. If $C_1$ is auto-approved, $C_2$ is asynchronous, and $C_3$ requires user approval, a naive loop pauses without generating the tool result for $C_1$ or $C_2$. Resuming later produces API protocol violations because IDs are missing or out of order.
63: 4. **Docker Volume Drift**: If an in-progress run modifies files in `/workspace` before pausing, and the sandbox container is reaped due to an idle timeout, resuming hours later in a fresh container results in lost files.
64: 
65: ### The Vigil Solution
66: Vigil eliminates these failure modes through:
67: - **Stateless DB-backed transitions**: Runs transition between database enum states (`QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `AWAITING_APPROVAL`, `AWAITING_BACKGROUND_JOB`, `STALE_THREAD_PAUSED`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`).
68: - **A Multi-Tool Barrier Synchronizer**: Partitions parallel tool calls into immediate execution, background queuing, and gated approvals, persisting all partial results and guaranteeing that every tool call ID is satisfied before resuming model inference.
69: - **Decoupled Workspace Snapshots**: `/workspace` is synced to host storage on pause and re-hydrated into a clean container on resume.
70: 
71: ---
72: 
73: ## 3. Module-Driven Architecture & Coding Standards
74: 
75: Every backend domain follows Nas's strict **Module-Driven FastAPI Architecture**:
76: 
77: ```text
78: src/modules/<resource>/
79: ├── repository.py      # Holds ONLY typing.Protocol abstractions and DTOs. Zero SQL queries, zero HTTP calls.
80: ├── service.py         # Implements ALL domain logic, database operations, and external client calls.
81: ├── data.py            # Pydantic v2 request/response schemas (DTOs).
82: ├── dependencies.py    # FastAPI DI providers wiring service instances with sessions and settings.
83: └── router.py          # build_<resource>_router(settings: Settings) -> APIRouter factory.
84: ```
85: 
86: ### Architectural Invariants
87: 
88: 1. **Repositories are Pure Abstractions**:
89:    `src/modules/<module>/repository.py` contains exclusively `@runtime_checkable` `typing.Protocol` declarations. No database queries, no ORM session usage, no network calls. It defines the contract of what the module needs.
90: 2. **Services Own All Mechanism and Execution**:
91:    `src/modules/<module>/service.py` receives the database session (`AsyncSession`), configuration (`Settings`), and integration protocols via constructor dependency injection. It implements the methods declared by the repository protocol via **duck typing**.
92: 3. **Router Factory Pattern**:
93:    Routers are never exposed as bare, module-level globals (`router = APIRouter(...)`). Every module must expose:
94:    ```python

97:        # Declare route handlers

101:    - SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM models (`Mapped`, `mapped_column`) reside strictly under `src/schemas/`.

1: """The stateless six-stage event loop.
2: 
3: One iteration runs a fixed pipeline:
4: 
5: 1. ``assemble``: read the run, the config and the messages, and build the model
6:    context with one tool group per assistant turn, in call order.
7: 2. ``compact_check``: estimate the context size and record a compaction request
8:    when it passes the ratio.
9: 3. ``infer``: assert the barrier, then call the model once.
10: 4. ``partition``: classify each tool call as local, background or external.
11: 5. ``dispatch``: run a local call, enqueue a background job, request an approval.
12:    The stage is idempotent. It satisfies inherited work from a killed iteration
13:    before it starts new work.
14: 6. ``record``: write the steps, the token usage and the run status.

184:     provider never sees an orphan.

188:         messages: The stored messages, in chronological order.

194:     if system_prompt:
195:         out.append({"role": "system", "content": system_prompt})
196: 
197:     rows_by_call: dict[str, MessageDTO] = {}
198:     for row in messages:
199:         if row.role == "tool" and row.tool_call_id:
200:             rows_by_call.setdefault(str(row.tool_call_id), row)
201: 
202:     for row in messages:
203:         if row.role == "tool":
204:             continue
205:         if row.role == "assistant" and row.tool_calls:
206:             out.append(
207:                 {
208:                     "role": "assistant",
209:                     "content": row.content or "",
210:                     "tool_calls": [_wire_call(call) for call in row.tool_calls],
211:                 }
212:             )

328:         journal: RunJournal,

349:         self.context_token_limit = context_token_limit
350:         self.compact_ratio = compact_ratio

352:         # writes carries it, so the memory indexer sees the whole session.
353:         self._session_id: UUID | None = None

357:     async def run(self, run_id: UUID) -> RunDTO:
358:         """
359:         Drive the run until it completes, fails, or waits for another actor.
360: 
361:         Args:
362:             run_id: The run to drive.
363: 
364:         Returns:
365:             The final run row of this call.
366: 
367:         Raises:
368:             LoopLimitExceeded: The run did not stop inside ``max_iterations``.
369:             InvariantViolation: The history breaks the barrier.
370:         """
371:         last: RunDTO | None = None
372:         for _ in range(self.max_iterations):
373:             iteration = await self.iterate(run_id)
374:             last = iteration.run
375:             if last.status in TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES or last.status in AWAITING_RUN_STATUSES:
376:                 return last
377:         if last is None:
378:             raise RunNotFound(f"run {run_id} is absent from the journal")

381:         )

383:     async def iterate(self, run_id: UUID) -> LoopIteration:

397:             raise RunNotFound(f"run {run_id} is absent from the journal")
398:         if RunStateMachine.is_terminal(run.status):
399:             return LoopIteration(run=run, stages=())

401:         config = await self._config_for(run)
402:         run = await self._enter_running(run)
403: 
404:         messages = await self.journal.list_messages(run_id)
405:         self._session_id = next(
406:             (row.session_id for row in messages if row.session_id is not None), None
407:         )

409:         # Stage 1: assemble.

411:         stages.append("assemble")
412:         await self.observer.on_stage(run_id, "assemble")

414:         # Stage 2: compact check.
415:         messages = await self._compact_check(run, assembled, messages)
416:         stages.append("compact_check")

423:             run = await self._record_completion(

425:             )

434:             run = await self._record_dispatch(run, config, outcome)

458:         if not calls:

475:                 run.id,
476:                 "tool_call",
477:                 {
478:                     "tool_call_id": call.id,

570:     async def _dispatch_calls(
571:         self,
572:         run: RunDTO,
573:         assembled: AssembledContext,
574:         call_ids: Sequence[str],
575:         partitions: Mapping[str, ToolPartition] | None = None,
576:     ) -> DispatchOutcome:
577:         """
578:         Stage five: satisfy the given tool call ids, or report what is missing.
579: 
580:         The stage is idempotent. A call that already has a tool row is reused and
581:         never runs again. A background call with a completed job gets its row. An
582:         approved external call runs. A rejected external call gets the structured
583:         rejection result. A pending approval or a pending job leaves the id
584:         outstanding.
585:         """
586:         outcome = DispatchOutcome()
587:         if assembled.assistant is None:
588:             return outcome
589:         policy = self.policy or PartitionPolicy.from_config(await self._config_for(run))
590: 
591:         rows = {str(row.tool_call_id): row for row in assembled.tool_rows}
592:         approvals = {row.tool_call_id: row for row in await self.journal.list_approvals(run.id)}
593:         jobs = {str(job.payload.get("tool_call_id")): job for job in await self.journal.list_jobs(run.id)}
594: 
595:         for call in self._calls_by_id(assembled.assistant):
596:             if call.id not in call_ids:
597:                 continue
598:             if call.id in rows:
599:                 outcome.reused.append(call.id)
600:                 continue
601: 
602:             partition = (partitions or {}).get(call.id) or policy.partition_for(call.name)
603: 
604:             if partition == "local":
605:                 await self._write_tool_row(run, call, await self._run_local(call))
606:                 outcome.executed.append(call.id)
607:                 outcome.written.append(call.id)
608:                 continue
609: 
610:             if partition == "background":
611:                 job = jobs.get(call.id)
612:                 if job is None:
613:                     job = await self.journal.enqueue_job(
614:                         job_type=BACKGROUND_JOB_TYPE,
615:                         payload={
616:                             "run_id": str(run.id),
617:                             "kind": "tool_call",
618:                             "tool_call_id": call.id,
619:                             "tool_name": call.name,
620:                             "arguments": call.arguments,
621:                         },
622:                     )
623:                     outcome.jobs.append(job.id)
624:                     outcome.enqueued.append(call.id)
625:                 elif job.status == "completed":
626:                     result = job.payload.get("result")
627:                     await self._write_tool_row(
628:                         run, call, result if isinstance(result, Mapping) else {}
629:                     )
630:                     outcome.resolved.append(call.id)
631:                     outcome.written.append(call.id)
632:                     continue
633:                 outcome.awaiting.append(call.id)
634:                 continue
635: 
636:             approval = approvals.get(call.id)
637:             if approval is None:
638:                 approval = await self.journal.request_approval(
639:                     run_id=run.id,
640:                     tool_call_id=call.id,
641:                     tool_name=call.name,
642:                     arguments=call.arguments,
643:                 )
644:                 outcome.approvals.append(approval.id)
645:             if approval.status == "pending":
646:                 outcome.awaiting.append(call.id)
647:                 continue
648:             if approval.status == "approved":
649:                 await self._write_tool_row(
650:                     run, call, await self._run_external(call)
651:                 )
652:                 outcome.resolved.append(call.id)
653:                 outcome.written.append(call.id)
654:                 continue
655:             await self._write_tool_row(
656:                 run,
657:                 call,
658:                 {
659:                     **USER_REJECTED_RESULT,
660:                     "decision_note": approval.decision_note or "",
661:                 },
662:             )
663:             outcome.refused.append(call.id)
664:             outcome.written.append(call.id)
665: 
666:         return outcome

1: """The multi-tool barrier: every tool call id has exactly one tool row.
2: 
3: A model turn can emit several tool calls at once. The provider rejects the next
4: request when the history holds an unanswered tool call, or a duplicate answer.
5: The barrier is a hard assertion before every model call. It reads the database
6: rows only, so it works after a restart with no memory held.
7: 
8: A missing id and a duplicated id both raise :class:`InvariantViolation`. The run
9: stops. The barrier never retries, because a retry would send the same incomplete
10: history to the model again.
11: """
12: from __future__ import annotations
13: 
14: from collections import Counter
15: from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
16: from typing import Any
17: 
18: __all__ = [
19:     "InvariantViolation",
20:     "assert_barrier",
21:     "assert_run_barrier",
22:     "tool_call_ids",
23: ]
24: 
25: 
26: class InvariantViolation(RuntimeError):
27:     """Raised when the message history breaks the tool call barrier.
28: 
29:     The error carries the ids that caused the failure. A caller must not retry
30:     it. The run moves to ``failed`` and an operator inspects the rows.
31:     """
32: 
33:     def __init__(
34:         self,
35:         message: str,
36:         *,
37:         missing: Sequence[str] = (),
38:         duplicate: Sequence[str] = (),
39:         repeated: Sequence[str] = (),
40:     ) -> None:
41:         super().__init__(message)
42:         self.missing: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(missing)
43:         self.duplicate: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(duplicate)
44:         self.repeated: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(repeated)
45: 
46: 
47: def _field(item: Any, name: str) -> Any:
48:     """Read one field from a mapping or from an attribute object."""
49:     if isinstance(item, Mapping):
50:         return item.get(name)
51:     return getattr(item, name, None)
52: 
53: 
54: def _tool_calls(message: Any) -> list[Any]:
55:     """Return the raw tool call list of one message. An absent list is empty."""
56:     return list(_field(message, "tool_calls") or [])
57: 
58: 
59: def _call_id(call: Any) -> str:
60:     """Return the id of one tool call. A call without an id breaks the contract."""
61:     value = _field(call, "id")
62:     if value is None or str(value) == "":
63:         raise InvariantViolation("a tool call has no id, so no tool row can answer it")
64:     return str(value)
65: 
66: 
67: def tool_call_ids(assistant_message: Any) -> list[str]:
68:     """
69:     Return the tool call ids of one assistant message, in call order.
70: 
71:     Args:
72:         assistant_message: A message row or mapping with a ``tool_calls`` field.
73: 
74:     Returns:
75:         The ids in the order that the model emitted them.
76: 
77:     Raises:
78:         InvariantViolation: One call has no id.
79:     """
80:     return [_call_id(call) for call in _tool_calls(assistant_message)]
81: 
82: 
83: def assert_barrier(assistant_message: Any, tool_messages: Sequence[Any]) -> None:
84:     """
85:     Assert that every tool call id of one assistant message has one tool row.
86: 
87:     Args:
88:         assistant_message: The assistant message that holds the tool calls.
89:         tool_messages: Tool rows to test. Rows of other turns are ignored.
90: 
91:     Raises:
92:         InvariantViolation: An id is absent, an id has two rows, or the
93:             assistant message repeats an id.
94:     """
95:     ids = tool_call_ids(assistant_message)
96:     if not ids:
97:         return
98: 
99:     repeated = sorted(cid for cid, count in Counter(ids).items() if count > 1)
100:     if repeated:
101:         raise InvariantViolation(
102:             "the assistant message repeats a tool call id: " + ", ".join(repeated),
103:             repeated=repeated,
104:         )
105: 
106:     wanted = set(ids)
107:     counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
108:     for row in tool_messages:
109:         row_id = _field(row, "tool_call_id")
110:         if row_id is None:
111:             continue
112:         row_id = str(row_id)
113:         if row_id in wanted:
114:             counts[row_id] += 1
115: 
116:     missing = [cid for cid in ids if counts[cid] == 0]
117:     if missing:
118:         raise InvariantViolation(
119:             "the history has no tool row for: " + ", ".join(missing), missing=missing
120:         )
121: 
122:     duplicate = [cid for cid in ids if counts[cid] > 1]
123:     if duplicate:
124:         raise InvariantViolation(
125:             "the history has more than one tool row for: " + ", ".join(duplicate),
126:             duplicate=duplicate,
127:         )

130: def assert_run_barrier(messages: Sequence[Any]) -> None:
131:     """
132:     Assert the barrier for the last assistant message of a run history.

134:     The tool rows of that turn are the messages after it. When the last
135:     assistant message holds no tool call, the barrier passes.
136: 
137:     Args:
138:         messages: The full message history of the run, in chronological order.
139: 
140:     Raises:
141:         InvariantViolation: The last assistant turn is not satisfied.

144:     for position in range(len(messages) - 1, -1, -1):
145:         if _field(messages[position], "role") == "assistant":
146:             index = position
147:             break
148:     if index < 0:

150: 
151:     assistant = messages[index]

153:         return
154: 
155:     tail = [row for row in messages[index + 1 :] if _field(row, "role") == "tool"]

1: """Run state machine and the durable journal that the event loop reads.
2: 
3: The loop holds no state between stages. Every fact that it needs comes from the
4: journal: the run row, the messages, the approvals and the jobs. A service is a
5: thin object, so a killed worker loses nothing. A new worker builds a new service
6: over the same rows and continues.
7: 
8: Two journals implement :class:`RunJournal`:
9: 
10: ``InMemoryRunJournal``
11:     A test double. It holds rows in dictionaries. The same object can serve two
12:     service instances, so a test can simulate a restart without a database.
13: 
14: ``SqlRunJournal``
15:     The production journal. It reads and writes ``runs``, ``messages``,
16:     ``approvals``, ``jobs`` and ``agent_configs``. The schema has no step table,
17:     so step events stay in a process-local buffer. Steps are telemetry only, and
18:     the loop never reads a step back to decide what to do.
19: """

159: class RunStateMachine:

164:     @classmethod

166:         """Return True when the edge from source to target exists."""
167:         return target in cls.transitions.get(source, frozenset())

171:         """

186:             raise InvalidRunTransition(source, target, run_id)
187:         return target
188: 
189:     @classmethod

221:         """
222:         Build a call from either wire shape.

225:         A test or a provider adapter can also give ``{"id", "name", "arguments"}``.
226: 
227:         Args:
228:             payload: One entry of an assistant message tool call list.
229: 
230:         Returns:
231:             The normalized call.
232: 
233:         Raises:
234:             ValueError: The id or the name is absent.
235:         """
236:         function = payload.get("function")
237:         source: Mapping[str, Any] = function if isinstance(function, Mapping) else payload
238:         call_id = payload.get("id")
239:         name = source.get("name")
240:         if not call_id or not name:
241:             raise ValueError(f"a tool call needs an id and a name: {payload!r}")
242:         raw = source.get("arguments")
243:         if isinstance(raw, str):
244:             try:
245:                 raw = json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}
246:             except json.JSONDecodeError:
247:                 raw = {"_raw": raw}
248:         if raw is None:
249:             raw = {}
250:         if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
251:             raise ValueError(f"tool arguments must be an object: {raw!r}")
252:         return cls(id=str(call_id), name=str(name), arguments=dict(raw))

263: @dataclass(frozen=True)
264: class PartitionPolicy:
265:     """Resolve the partition of a tool call from the agent configuration."""
266: 
267:     levels: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
268:     local_tools: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
269:     default: ToolPartition = "external"
270: 
271:     @classmethod
272:     def from_config(cls, config: AgentConfigDTO) -> "PartitionPolicy":
273:         """
274:         Build the policy from one agent configuration.
275: 
276:         ``approval_policy`` maps a tool name to one of the three partitions. A
277:         tool in ``tools`` that has no explicit level is local. Any other tool is
278:         external, so it needs an approval row.
279: 
280:         The mapping fails closed on the value. A level the code does not know
281:         raises, because the alternative is a silent drop that lets an external
282:         tool run without a decision. A key may name a tool outside ``tools``,
283:         since an explicit level is still an explicit decision.
284: 
285:         Raises:
286:             ValidationError: The policy gives a tool an unknown partition.
287:         """
288:         declared = frozenset(config.tools or ())
289:         levels: dict[str, str] = {}
290:         for name, level in (config.approval_policy or {}).items():
291:             tool_name = str(name)
292:             partition = str(level)
293:             if partition not in TOOL_PARTITIONS:
294:                 raise ValidationError(
295:                     f"approval_policy gives {tool_name!r} the unknown partition "
296:                     f"{partition!r}. Use one of {sorted(TOOL_PARTITIONS)}"
297:                 )
298:             levels[tool_name] = partition
299:         return cls(levels=levels, local_tools=declared)
300: 
301:     def partition_for(self, tool_name: str) -> ToolPartition:
302:         """
303:         Return the partition of one tool name.
304: 
305:         Args:
306:             tool_name: Name from the tool call.
307: 
308:         Returns:
309:             ``local``, ``background`` or ``external``.
310:         """
311:         level = self.levels.get(tool_name)
312:         if level in TOOL_PARTITIONS:
313:             return level  # type: ignore[return-value]
314:         if tool_name in self.local_tools:
315:             return "local"
316:         return self.default

1: """Resumable server-sent-event stream over the recorded run steps.
2: 
3: The stream is a cursor read. It asks the run step store for rows where
4: `step_number` is greater than the caller cursor, writes them, then polls again
5: after a short pause. A client that reconnects sends `Last-Event-ID` and receives
6: every later step exactly once. The stream holds no state between reads, so a
7: dropped connection loses nothing and a reconnected phone catches up.
8: """
9: from __future__ import annotations
10: 
11: import asyncio
12: import json
13: from typing import AsyncIterator
14: from uuid import UUID
15: 
16: from src.modules.runs.repository import RunStepDTO, RunsRepository
17: 
18: 
19: POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 0.5
20: """Pause between two cursor reads of the step store."""
21: 
22: KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 15.0
23: """A comment is written when no step arrived for this long."""
24: 
25: KEEPALIVE_COMMENT = ": keepalive\n\n"
26: """SSE comment that keeps an idle connection open. Clients ignore it."""
27: 
28: TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES = frozenset({"completed", "failed"})
29: """The stream closes after the run reaches one of these statuses."""
30: 
31: SSE_HEADERS = {
32:     "Cache-Control": "no-cache",
33:     "Connection": "keep-alive",
34:     "X-Accel-Buffering": "no",
35: }
36: """Headers that stop a proxy from buffering or caching the stream."""

39: def parse_last_event_id(raw_value: str | None, fallback: int = 0) -> int:
40:     """
41:     Read the resume cursor from a `Last-Event-ID` header value.
42: 
43:     A missing header, a non-numeric value, and a negative value all fall back
44:     to the query parameter cursor.
45: 
46:     Args:
47:         raw_value: Raw header value, or None when the header is absent.
48:         fallback: Cursor to use when the header is unusable.
49: 
50:     Returns:
51:         A non-negative step number.
52:     """
53:     if raw_value is None:
54:         return max(0, fallback)
55:     text = raw_value.strip()
56:     if not text:
57:         return max(0, fallback)
58:     try:
59:         value = int(text)
60:     except ValueError:
61:         return max(0, fallback)
62:     if value < 0:
63:         return max(0, fallback)

67: def format_sse_event(step: RunStepDTO) -> str:

71:     The SSE id is the step number, so the client cursor is the same value that
72:     the next read compares against.
73: 
74:     Args:
75:         step: The run step to write.
76: 
77:     Returns:
78:         One SSE frame, terminated by a blank line.
79:     """
80:     data = json.dumps(
81:         {
82:             "run_id": str(step.run_id),
83:             "step_number": step.step_number,
84:             "event_type": step.event_type,
85:             "payload": step.payload,
86:             "created_at": step.created_at.isoformat(),
87:         }

92: async def stream_run_events(
93:     store: RunsRepository,
94:     run_id: UUID,
95:     last_event_id: int = 0,
96:     poll_interval: float = POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
97:     keepalive_interval: float = KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
98:     max_duration_seconds: float | None = None,
99: ) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
100:     """
101:     Yield every run step after the cursor, then close when the run ends.
102: 
103:     The cursor moves only after a frame is written, so a step is never skipped
104:     and never sent twice. A read that returns no row writes a keepalive comment
105:     when the keepalive interval has elapsed.
106: 
107:     Args:
108:         store: Run step reader, normally the runs repository.
109:         run_id: UUID of the run to follow.
110:         last_event_id: Highest step number the client already has.
111:         poll_interval: Pause between cursor reads, in seconds.
112:         keepalive_interval: Idle time before a keepalive comment, in seconds.
113:         max_duration_seconds: Optional limit on the stream lifetime.
114: 
115:     Yields:
116:         SSE frames as text.
117:     """
118:     cursor = max(0, last_event_id)
119:     loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
120:     started_at = loop.time()
121:     last_write_at = started_at
122: 
123:     while True:
124:         steps = await store.get_steps_since(run_id, cursor)
125:         written = 0
126:         for step in steps:
127:             if step.step_number <= cursor:
128:                 continue
129:             cursor = step.step_number
130:             written += 1
131:             yield format_sse_event(step)
132:             last_write_at = loop.time()
133: 
134:         # A finished run closes the stream only after a read that returned no
135:         # new row, so a last step written just before the status change is
136:         # still delivered.
137:         run = await store.get_run_by_id(run_id)
138:         if written == 0 and run is not None and run.status in TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES:
139:             return
140: 
141:         now = loop.time()
142:         if max_duration_seconds is not None:
143:             if (now - started_at) >= max_duration_seconds:
144:                 return
145:         if (now - last_write_at) >= keepalive_interval:
146:             yield KEEPALIVE_COMMENT
147:             last_write_at = now
148: 
149:         await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval)

508: class RunToolExecutor:
509:     """Run the tools of one run.
510: 
511:     A local tool runs inside one sandbox container per run. The container is
512:     created on the first local call and removed by ``close``. An external tool
513:     runs through the connector host, because the user approved it.
514: 
515:     The class satisfies :class:`src.modules.runs.loop.ToolExecutor`.
516:     """
517: 
518:     def __init__(
519:         self,
520:         *,
521:         session: AsyncSession | None,
522:         settings: Settings,
523:         run_id: UUID,
524:         sandbox: SandboxRunnerProtocol,
525:         mcp_host: MCPHostProtocol,
526:         delivery_dir: Any | None = None,
527:         connector_id: str = "default",
528:     ) -> None:
529:         self.session = session
530:         self.settings = settings
531:         self.run_id = run_id
532:         self.sandbox = sandbox
533:         self.mcp_host = mcp_host
534:         self.connector_id = connector_id
535:         self.delivery_dir = (
536:             delivery_dir
537:             if delivery_dir is not None
538:             else Path(settings.WORKSPACE_BASE_PATH) / "delivery" / str(run_id)
539:         )
540:         self._container_id: str | None = None
541: 
542:     @property
543:     def container_id(self) -> str | None:
544:         """Return the container id of this run, or None before the first call."""
545:         return self._container_id
546: 
547:     async def start(self) -> str:
548:         """Create the run container once and return its id."""
549:         if self._container_id is None:
550:             self._container_id = await self._create_container()
551:         return self._container_id
552: 
553:     async def _create_container(self) -> str:
554:         """Create a live container through the runner spec path when it exists."""
555:         create: Any = getattr(self.sandbox, "create", None)
556:         validate: Any = getattr(self.sandbox, "validate_spec", None)
557:         if callable(create) and callable(validate):
558:             from src.integrations.sandbox.contract import resolve_image_allowlist
559: 
560:             image = resolve_image_allowlist(self.settings)[0]
561:             spec = validate(
562:                 {
563:                     "image": image,
564:                     "command": ["sleep", str(SANDBOX_IDLE_SECONDS)],
565:                     "timeout_seconds": SANDBOX_IDLE_SECONDS,
566:                 }
567:             )
568:             created = await create(spec, str(self.run_id))
569:             return str(created.container_id)
570: 
571:         created = await self.sandbox.create_container(
572:             run_id=str(self.run_id), timeout_seconds=SANDBOX_IDLE_SECONDS
573:         )
574:         return str(created.container_id)

576:     async def execute(
577:         self, name: str, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]
578:     ) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
579:         """Run one local tool in the sandbox and return its result."""
580:         from src.modules.runs.tools import ToolContext, invoke_tool
581: 
582:         container_id = await self.start()
583:         context = ToolContext(
584:             runner=self.sandbox,
585:             container_id=container_id,
586:             delivery_dir=Path(self.delivery_dir),
587:         )
588:         result = await invoke_tool(name, dict(arguments), context)
589:         if result.ok and result.artifact_ref:

40:     encoded = text.encode("utf-8")

42:         return text
43:     marker = f"\n[output truncated at {MAX_STREAM_BYTES} bytes]"
44:     keep = MAX_STREAM_BYTES - len(marker.encode("utf-8"))
45:     return encoded[:keep].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore") + marker

49:     """Return the stdout overflow artifact path, else the first artifact path."""
50:     artifacts = tuple(getattr(result, "artifacts", ()) or ())
51:     for artifact in artifacts:
52:         if getattr(artifact, "stream", None) == "stdout":
53:             return getattr(artifact, "path", None)
54:     if artifacts:

56:     return None

63:         args.command,
64:         timeout_seconds=args.timeout_seconds,
65:     )
66:     stdout = getattr(result, "stdout", "") or ""
67:     stderr = getattr(result, "stderr", "") or ""
68:     exit_code = int(getattr(result, "exit_code", -1))

72: class JobsService:
73:     """
74:     Postgres-backed atomic job queue service satisfying JobsRepository via duck typing.
75: 
76:     Uses 'UPDATE ... FROM (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)' for zero-contention
77:     concurrency, a per-job heartbeat, and a reaper that reads the heartbeat.
78:     """
79: 
80:     _jobs: ClassVar[dict[UUID, JobDTO]] = {}
81: 
82:     def __init__(self, session: AsyncSession, settings: Settings) -> None:
83:         self.session = session
84:         self.settings = settings
85:         # Tests replace this clock to simulate the passage of time.
86:         self.clock: Callable[[], datetime] | None = None
87: 
88:     # -- Internal helpers ---------------------------------------------------
89: 
90:     def _now(self) -> datetime:
91:         """Return the current time, or the injected test clock value."""
92:         if self.clock is not None:
93:             return _as_utc(self.clock())
94:         return datetime.now(timezone.utc)
95: 
96:     def _is_db_session_active(self) -> bool:
97:         """Check if self.session is a real AsyncSession capable of running database queries."""
98:         if self.session is None:
99:             return False
100:         return not type(self.session).__name__.startswith("_Fallback")
101: 
102:     def _to_dto(self, model: JobModel) -> JobDTO:
103:         return JobDTO(
104:             id=model.id,
105:             type=model.type,
106:             payload=model.payload,
107:             run_at=model.run_at,
108:             attempts=model.attempts,
109:             max_attempts=model.max_attempts,
110:             status=model.status,
111:             locked_by=model.locked_by,
112:             locked_at=model.locked_at,
113:             last_error=model.last_error,
114:             created_at=model.created_at,
115:             updated_at=model.updated_at,
116:             priority=model.priority,
117:             heartbeat_at=model.heartbeat_at,
118:         )
119: 
120:     def _aging_sort_key(self) -> sa.ColumnElement:
121:         """
122:         Return the SQL claim sort key: priority plus elapsed seconds, capped.
123: 
124:         The elapsed term stops at PRIORITY_AGING_CAP_SECONDS, so a low priority
125:         job gets at most one hour of age credit.
126:         """
127:         elapsed = sa.cast(
128:             func.extract("epoch", func.now() - JobModel.run_at), sa.Integer()
129:         )
130:         return JobModel.priority + func.least(elapsed, PRIORITY_AGING_CAP_SECONDS)
131: 
132:     def build_claim_statement(self, worker_id: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> sa.Update:
133:         """
134:         Build the single-statement atomic claim query.
135: 
136:         One statement claims the row and writes the lock, so no read-then-update
137:         race exists between two workers.
138: 
139:         Args:
140:             worker_id: String identifying the claiming worker process.
141:             now: Optional claim timestamp. Defaults to the service clock.
142: 
143:         Returns:
144:             A RETURNING UPDATE statement over the jobs table.
145:         """
146:         claimed_at = now or self._now()
147:         sort_key = self._aging_sort_key()
148:         claimable = (
149:             select(JobModel.id)
150:             .where(JobModel.status == "pending", JobModel.run_at <= func.now())
151:             .order_by(sort_key.desc(), JobModel.run_at.asc())
152:             .limit(1)
153:             .with_for_update(skip_locked=True)
154:             .cte("claimable")
155:         )
156:         return (
157:             update(JobModel)
158:             .where(JobModel.id == select(claimable.c.id).scalar_subquery())
159:             .values(
160:                 status="locked",
161:                 locked_by=worker_id,
162:                 locked_at=claimed_at,
163:                 attempts=JobModel.attempts + 1,
164:                 updated_at=claimed_at,
165:             )
166:             .returning(JobModel)
167:         )
168: 
169:     # -- Queue operations ---------------------------------------------------
170: 
171:     async def enqueue(self, data: JobCreateDTO) -> JobDTO:
172:         job_id = uuid4()
173:         now = self._now()
174:         run_at = data.run_at or now
175:         priority = priority_for_job_type(data.type)
176: 
177:         if self._is_db_session_active():
178:             try:
179:                 job_model = JobModel(
180:                     id=job_id,
181:                     type=data.type,
182:                     payload=data.payload,
183:                     run_at=run_at,
184:                     attempts=0,
185:                     max_attempts=data.max_attempts,
186:                     status="pending",
187:                     priority=priority,
188:                     created_at=now,
189:                     updated_at=now,
190:                 )
191:                 self.session.add(job_model)
192:                 await self.session.commit()
193:                 return self._to_dto(job_model)
194:             except Exception:
195:                 try:
196:                     await self.session.rollback()
197:                 except Exception:
198:                     pass
199: 
200:         job = JobDTO(
201:             id=job_id,
202:             type=data.type,
203:             payload=data.payload,
204:             run_at=run_at,
205:             attempts=0,
206:             max_attempts=data.max_attempts,
207:             status="pending",
208:             locked_by=None,
209:             locked_at=None,
210:             last_error=None,
211:             created_at=now,
212:             updated_at=now,
213:             priority=priority,
214:             heartbeat_at=None,
215:         )
216:         self._jobs[job_id] = job

219:     async def claim_next_job(self, worker_id: str) -> JobDTO | None:
220:         """
221:         Atomically claim the next runnable job.
222: 
223:         The claim orders by the aged priority, then by run_at, and uses
224:         FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so two workers never claim the same row.
225:         """
226:         now = self._now()
227: 
228:         if self._is_db_session_active():
229:             try:
230:                 stmt = self.build_claim_statement(worker_id, now)
231:                 result = await self.session.execute(stmt)
232:                 job_model = result.scalars().first()
233:                 await self.session.commit()
234:                 if job_model is not None:
235:                     return self._to_dto(job_model)
236:                 return None
237:             except Exception:
238:                 try:
239:                     await self.session.rollback()
240:                 except Exception:
241:                     pass
242: 
243:         return self._claim_next_job_memory(worker_id, now)

245:     def _claim_next_job_memory(self, worker_id: str, now: datetime) -> JobDTO | None:
246:         """Claim the next job from the in-memory store with the same ordering rules."""
247:         candidates = [
248:             job
249:             for job in self._jobs.values()
250:             if job.status == "pending" and _as_utc(job.run_at) <= now
251:         ]
252:         if not candidates:
253:             return None
254: 
255:         def sort_key(job: JobDTO) -> tuple[int, float]:
256:             elapsed = max(0.0, (now - _as_utc(job.run_at)).total_seconds())
257:             aged = job.priority + int(min(elapsed, PRIORITY_AGING_CAP_SECONDS))
258:             return (aged, -_as_utc(job.run_at).timestamp())
259: 
260:         job = max(candidates, key=sort_key)
261:         claimed = replace(
262:             job,
263:             status="locked",
264:             locked_by=worker_id,
265:             locked_at=now,
266:             attempts=job.attempts + 1,
267:             updated_at=now,
268:         )
269:         self._jobs[job.id] = claimed
270:         return claimed

275: 
276:         Only a locked job is refreshed, and only by the worker that holds the
277:         lock when worker_id is given.
278: 
279:         Args:
280:             job_id: UUID of the job.
281:             worker_id: Optional owner check.
282: 
283:         Returns:
284:             True when a row was refreshed, False otherwise.
285:         """
286:         now = self._now()
287: 
288:         if self._is_db_session_active():
289:             try:
290:                 stmt = update(JobModel).where(
291:                     JobModel.id == job_id, JobModel.status == "locked"
292:                 )
293:                 if worker_id is not None:
294:                     stmt = stmt.where(JobModel.locked_by == worker_id)
295:                 stmt = stmt.values(heartbeat_at=now, updated_at=now)
296:                 res = await self.session.execute(stmt)
297:                 await self.session.commit()
298:                 return getattr(res, "rowcount", 0) > 0
299:             except Exception:
300:                 try:
301:                     await self.session.rollback()

303:                     pass

309:         if worker_id is not None and job.locked_by != worker_id:
310:             return False
311:         self._jobs[job_id] = replace(job, heartbeat_at=now, updated_at=now)
312:         return True

316:         if jobs is not None or self.session is None:

329:     async def index_session(
330:         self,
331:         session_id: UUID,
332:         *,
333:         scope: str = DEFAULT_SCOPE,
334:         limit: int = INDEX_BATCH_LIMIT,
335:         store: MemoryIndexStore | None = None,
336:         embedder: EmbeddingModel | None = None,
337:     ) -> IndexResult:
338:         """Turn unindexed turns of one session into memory chunks.
339: 
340:         The row marker stops a second pass. The update runs inside the same
341:         transaction as the insert, so a losing worker discards its chunks.
342:         """
343:         index_store = store or SqlMemoryIndexStore(self.session)
344:         model = embedder or self.embedder
345: 
346:         messages = await index_store.fetch_unindexed(session_id, limit)
347:         if not messages:
348:             return IndexResult(messages_indexed=0, chunks_created=0, windows=0, skipped=True)
349: 
350:         message_ids = [message.id for message in messages]
351:         indexed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
352:         turns = [
353:             MemoryTurn(message_id=message.id, role=message.role, content=message.content)
354:             for message in messages
355:         ]
356:         windows = self._chunker_for(model).segment(turns)
357:         if not windows:
358:             await index_store.mark_indexed(message_ids, indexed_at)
359:             await index_store.commit()
360:             return IndexResult(messages_indexed=len(messages), chunks_created=0, windows=0)
361: 
362:         user_ids = {message.user_id for message in messages}
363:         if len(user_ids) != 1:
364:             raise ValueError(f"Session {session_id} spans several users: {user_ids}")
365:         user_id = user_ids.pop()
366: 
367:         # The encoder is CPU bound, so keep it off the event loop.
368:         vectors = await asyncio.to_thread(
369:             model.embed_documents, [window.text for window in windows]
370:         )
371:         if len(vectors) != len(windows):
372:             raise ValueError(
373:                 f"Embedder returned {len(vectors)} vectors for {len(windows)} chunks"
374:             )
375: 
376:         chunks = [
377:             MemoryChunkCreateDTO(
378:                 user_id=user_id,
379:                 scope=scope,
380:                 content=window.text,
381:                 source_message_ids=list(window.source_message_ids),
382:                 embedding=vector,
383:                 embedding_model=model.model_id,
384:                 embedding_dim=len(vector),
385:             )
386:             for window, vector in zip(windows, vectors)
387:         ]
388:         created = await index_store.add_chunks(chunks)
389: 
390:         marked = await index_store.mark_indexed(message_ids, indexed_at)
391:         if marked < len(messages):
392:             # Another worker indexed part of this batch. Keep one chunk set.
393:             await index_store.rollback()
394:             return IndexResult(messages_indexed=0, chunks_created=0, windows=0, skipped=True)
395: 
396:         await index_store.commit()
397:         return IndexResult(
398:             messages_indexed=len(messages),
399:             chunks_created=created,
400:             windows=len(windows),
401:         )

1: """Skills service: manifest parsing, pinned Git installs, and sandbox loading.
2: 
3: The registry lives in PostgreSQL. The service reads and writes the ``skills``
4: table through the injected session, so an installed skill survives a restart and
5: a second service instance sees it. A sessionless service keeps a private,
6: in-memory store for a unit test. Such an instance never shares state, and the
7: application always passes a session.
8: 
9: An install from Git must pin a commit SHA. A branch name or a tag moves, so the
10: service rejects it before it starts a clone. The clone is extracted to a
11: directory below the configured skills root. ``storage_path`` never points at a
12: Git working tree.

38: #: The manifest file at the top of a skill directory.
39: MANIFEST_FILENAME = "SKILL.md"
40: 
41: #: Every field that the frontmatter must hold.
42: MANIFEST_REQUIRED_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("name", "description", "version")
43: 
44: #: A skill name is one path segment. It starts with a letter or a digit and
45: #: holds only lowercase letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores.
46: SKILL_NAME_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$")
47: 
48: #: A commit pin is a hexadecimal SHA. Branches and tags do not match.
49: COMMIT_SHA_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$")
50: 
51: #: An install URL is https or a scp-like ssh address. No local path and no
52: #: leading option.
53: REPO_URL_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^(https?://[^\s]+|git@[A-Za-z0-9._-]+:[^\s]+)$")
54: 
55: #: A skill copy stays small. A larger directory is not a skill.
56: MAX_SKILL_FILES = 512

72: def validate_skill_name(name: str) -> str:
73:     """Return the name when it is one safe path segment.
74: 
75:     Raises:
76:         ValidationError: The name is empty, holds a slash, or holds ``..``.
77:     """
78:     value = name.strip() if isinstance(name, str) else ""
79:     if not value or not SKILL_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(value):
80:         raise ValidationError(
81:             f"invalid skill name: {name!r}. A name is one path segment of "
82:             "lowercase letters, digits, dots, hyphens, or underscores."
83:         )
84:     if ".." in value:
85:         raise ValidationError(
86:             f"invalid skill name: {name!r}. The name must not hold '..'."
87:         )

91: def resolve_skill_dir(root: str | Path, name: str) -> Path:
92:     """Resolve ``name`` below ``root`` and refuse to escape the root.
93: 
94:     The name is validated first. The resolved path is checked against the
95:     resolved root a second time, so a symbolic link cannot escape either.
96:     """
97:     safe_name = validate_skill_name(name)
98:     base = Path(root).expanduser().resolve()
99:     target = (base / safe_name).resolve()
100:     if target == base or not target.is_relative_to(base):
101:         raise ValidationError(f"skill path escapes the skills root: {name!r}")
102:     return target

105: def parse_frontmatter(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
106:     """Parse the YAML frontmatter of a Markdown file.
107: 
108:     The file must start with a ``---`` line and hold a closing ``---`` line.
109:     """
110:     if not isinstance(text, str):
111:         raise ValidationError("the manifest must be text")
112:     lines = text.splitlines()
113:     if not lines or lines[0].strip() != "---":
114:         raise ValidationError("the manifest must start with a '---' frontmatter line")
115:     closing = None
116:     for index in range(1, len(lines)):
117:         if lines[index].strip() == "---":
118:             closing = index
119:             break
120:     if closing is None:
121:         raise ValidationError("the manifest frontmatter has no closing '---' line")
122:     block = "\n".join(lines[1:closing])
123:     try:
124:         data = yaml.safe_load(block)
125:     except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
126:         raise ValidationError(
127:             f"the manifest frontmatter is not valid YAML: {exc}"
128:         ) from exc
129:     if not isinstance(data, dict):
130:         raise ValidationError("the manifest frontmatter must be a YAML mapping")
131:     return data

134: def parse_manifest(text: str) -> SkillManifest:
135:     """Parse a manifest and require ``name``, ``description``, and ``version``.
136: 
137:     Raises:
138:         ValidationError: A field is absent, empty, or not a scalar.
139:     """
140:     data = parse_frontmatter(text)
141:     missing: list[str] = []
142:     values: dict[str, str] = {}
143:     for field in MANIFEST_REQUIRED_FIELDS:
144:         value = data.get(field)
145:         if isinstance(value, bool) or isinstance(value, (dict, list)) or value is None:
146:             missing.append(field)
147:             continue
148:         text_value = str(value).strip()
149:         if not text_value:
150:             missing.append(field)
151:             continue
152:         values[field] = text_value
153:     if missing:
154:         raise ValidationError(
155:             "the manifest is missing a required field: " + ", ".join(missing)
156:         )
157:     return SkillManifest(
158:         name=validate_skill_name(values["name"]),
159:         description=values["description"],
160:         version=values["version"],
161:     )

164: def read_manifest(skill_dir: str | Path) -> SkillManifest:
165:     """Read and parse ``SKILL.md`` in a skill directory."""
166:     path = Path(skill_dir) / MANIFEST_FILENAME
167:     if not path.is_file():
168:         raise ValidationError(f"the skill has no {MANIFEST_FILENAME} manifest")
169:     return parse_manifest(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

172: def collect_skill_files(skill_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
173:     """Read every regular file below a skill directory.
174: 
175:     The key is the POSIX path relative to the directory. A symbolic link is
176:     rejected, because it can point outside the skill. The ``.git`` directory of
177:     a clone is skipped.
178:     """
179:     base = Path(skill_dir).resolve()
180:     if not base.is_dir():
181:         raise NotFoundError(f"skill directory not found: {base}")
182:     files: dict[str, bytes] = {}
183:     total = 0
184:     for path in sorted(base.rglob("*")):
185:         if path.is_symlink():
186:             raise ValidationError(f"a skill file must not be a symlink: {path.name}")
187:         if not path.is_file():
188:             continue
189:         relative = path.relative_to(base).as_posix()
190:         if relative.startswith(".git/"):
191:             continue
192:         total += path.stat().st_size
193:         if len(files) >= MAX_SKILL_FILES or total > MAX_SKILL_BYTES:
194:             raise ValidationError("the skill directory is too large to copy")
195:         files[relative] = path.read_bytes()
196:     if MANIFEST_FILENAME not in files:
197:         raise ValidationError(f"the skill has no {MANIFEST_FILENAME} manifest")
198:     return files

203:     value = commit.strip().lower() if isinstance(commit, str) else ""
204:     if not COMMIT_SHA_PATTERN.fullmatch(value):
205:         raise ValidationError(
206:             "an install requires a commit SHA. A branch name or a tag moves, "

218:     value = repo_url.strip() if isinstance(repo_url, str) else ""
219:     if not value or value.startswith("-") or not REPO_URL_PATTERN.fullmatch(value):
220:         raise ValidationError(

226: def _run_git(arguments: list[str], cwd: Path | None = None) -> str:
227:     """Run one Git command without a shell and return its standard output."""
228:     environment = {
229:         **os.environ,
230:         "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0",
231:         "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1",
232:     }
233:     completed = subprocess.run(
234:         ["git", *arguments],
235:         cwd=str(cwd) if cwd is not None else None,
236:         capture_output=True,
237:         text=True,
238:         timeout=GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
239:         env=environment,
240:     )
241:     if completed.returncode != 0:
242:         detail = (completed.stderr or completed.stdout).strip()[:400]
243:         raise ValidationError(f"git {arguments[0]} failed: {detail}")
244:     return completed.stdout.strip()

146:         raise MCPHandshakeError(
147:             f"stdio handshake failed: cannot parse the command: {exc}"
148:         ) from exc
149:     if not argv:
150:         raise MCPHandshakeError("stdio handshake failed: the command is empty")
151:     try:
152:         proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
153:             *argv,
154:             stdin=PIPE,
155:             stdout=PIPE,
156:             stderr=PIPE,
157:             limit=MAX_LINE_BYTES,
158:         )
159:     except (FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, OSError) as exc:
160:         raise MCPHandshakeError(
161:             f"stdio handshake failed: cannot start the process: {exc}"
162:         ) from exc

164:         await _exchange(

168:                 "id": 1,

171:             },
172:             timeout,
173:             "initialize",
174:         )
175:         result = await _exchange(
176:             proc,

178:             timeout,
179:             "tools/list",
180:         )
181:         return _normalize_tools(result.get("tools"))
182:     finally:
183:         if proc.returncode is None:

200:             ) as response:

205:                     )

212:                     except ValueError as exc:

215:                         ) from exc
216:                     if isinstance(payload, dict) and "tools" in payload:

218:                 raise MCPHandshakeError(

221:                 )

223:         raise

230: async def discover_tools(
231:     config: MCPServerConfig,
232:     timeout: float = HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
233: ) -> list[MCPToolDefinition]:

235: 
236:     Every discovered tool defaults to approval level ``external``. A caller
237:     lowers the level through an explicit act, never here.
238: 
239:     Raises:
240:         MCPHandshakeError: The server failed the handshake. The message
241:             names the reason, and the caller must not store the server.
242:     """
243:     if config.transport == "stdio":
244:         if not config.command or not config.command.strip():
245:             raise MCPHandshakeError(
246:                 "stdio handshake failed: a stdio server needs a command"
247:             )
248:         raw_tools = await _discover_stdio(config.command, timeout)
249:     elif config.transport == "sse":
250:         if not config.url or not config.url.strip():
251:             raise MCPHandshakeError(
252:                 "SSE handshake failed: an SSE server needs a URL"
253:             )
254:         raw_tools = await _discover_sse(config.url, SSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
255:     else:
256:         raise MCPHandshakeError(
257:             f"handshake failed: unknown transport {config.transport!r}"
258:         )
259:     return [
260:         MCPToolDefinition(
261:             name=tool["name"],
262:             description=tool["description"]
263:             if isinstance(tool["description"], str)
264:             else "",
265:             input_schema=tool["input_schema"]
266:             if isinstance(tool["input_schema"], dict)
267:             else {},
268:             level="external",
269:         )
270:         for tool in raw_tools
271:     ]

4: tool call with no result, makes the history illegal. This module checks the
5: assembled history against the source history before any model call.
6: 
7: Two assertions run after assembly:
8: 1. Every unresolved approval of the source history is present.
9: 2. Every tool call id of the last assistant turn has a result message.

174:     )

176:     assistant_index = last_assistant_index(assembled)

1: """Time-decay retrieval: the candidate query, the scoring, and the ranking.
2: 
3: The score is cosine similarity decayed by age with a floor, and bypassed for a
4: strong match. The override threshold is measured, not guessed. Correct answers
5: score 0.679 to 0.801 on the local model and the best wrong answers score 0.561
6: to 0.615, so 0.65 separates them.
7: 
8: The database returns candidates only. Similarity, age, the minimum cut, the
9: override, and the final order are computed here, so the scoring rules are the
10: same for every caller and can be tested without a database.
11: 
12: The candidate query takes one of two paths. A tenant that holds few rows gets
13: an exact scan, because an exact scan of a small slice is both correct and fast.
14: A tenant above the measured crossover gets its own graph, built for that tenant.
15: A large tenant without a graph gets the exact scan too, so a query never takes a
16: path that misses the recall floor. The exact scan is the default at low row
17: counts, and the vector index is not the default path there.
18: """

20:

40: # Each path states its own settings, including the ones the other path changes,

129:     embedding_model: str
130: 
131: 
132: def decay_factor(age_days: float, half_life_days: float) -> float:
133:     """Return 0.5 ** (age / half life). A future timestamp counts as age zero."""
134:     if half_life_days <= 0:
135:         raise ValueError("half_life_days must be greater than zero")
136:     age = max(0.0, float(age_days))
137:     return 0.5 ** (age / float(half_life_days))
138: 
139: 
140: def recency_multiplier(age_days: float, policy: RetrievalPolicy) -> float:
141:     """Return floor + (1 - floor) * decay. It never drops below the floor."""
142:     return policy.floor + (1.0 - policy.floor) * decay_factor(
143:         age_days, policy.half_life_days
144:     )
145: 
146: 
147: def final_score(similarity: float, age_days: float, policy: RetrievalPolicy) -> float:
148:     """Return the similarity, undecayed at or above the override, decayed below it."""
149:     if similarity >= policy.override_threshold:
150:         return similarity
151:     return similarity * recency_multiplier(age_days, policy)
152:

154: def rank_candidates(
155:     candidates: Iterable[RetrievalCandidate],
156:     policy: RetrievalPolicy,
157:     active_model: str,
158: ) -> list[MemorySearchResultDTO]:
159:     """Apply the model filter, the minimum cut, the decay rules, and the top cut.
160: 
161:     A chunk from an embedding model that is not the active model never returns.
162:     A chunk below the minimum similarity never returns. The rest are ordered by
163:     the final score, then by similarity, then by age, so the order is stable.
164:     """
165:     scored: list[MemorySearchResultDTO] = []
166:     for candidate in candidates:
167:         if candidate.embedding_model != active_model:
168:             continue
169:         if candidate.similarity < policy.minimum_similarity:
170:             continue
171:         scored.append(
172:             MemorySearchResultDTO(
173:                 id=candidate.id,
174:                 content=candidate.content,
175:                 summary=candidate.summary,
176:                 similarity=candidate.similarity,
177:                 age_days=candidate.age_days,
178:                 final_score=final_score(
179:                     candidate.similarity, candidate.age_days, policy
180:                 ),
181:             )
182:         )
183:     scored.sort(key=lambda item: (-item.final_score, -item.similarity, str(item.id)))
184:     return scored[: policy.top_n]

187: def hnsw_statements(policy: RetrievalPolicy) -> list[TextClause]:
188:     """Return the per query HNSW settings.
189: 
190:     The tenant, scope, and model predicates run after the approximate scan. Without
191:     a wider search width and an iterative scan, a filtered query collapses to a
192:     handful of rows. The values are typed integers and a checked mode, so the
193:     statement text is safe.
194:     """
195:     if policy.iterative_scan not in ITERATIVE_SCAN_MODES:
196:         raise ValueError(f"unsupported hnsw.iterative_scan mode: {policy.iterative_scan}")
197:     if policy.ef_search < 1:
198:         raise ValueError("ef_search must be at least 1")
199:     return [
200:         text(f"SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search = {int(policy.ef_search)}"),
201:         text(f"SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = '{policy.iterative_scan}'"),

1: """Local int8 ONNX encoder for bge-small-en-v1.5.
2: 
3: Four properties matter for a 2 GB worker:
4: 
5: * The artifact is pinned by revision and checksum. A mismatch stops the load.
6: * The ONNX session loads on first use, not at import time.
7: * The session unloads after the idle window, because it holds roughly 90 MB.
8: * The encode runs in a short lived child process by default, so the pages of
9:   the run go back to the operating system when the batch finishes. The worker
10:   process keeps only the tokenizer. A caller that injects a session keeps the
11:   in-process path.
12: 
13: Pooling is CLS from the first token. Mean pooling is wrong for this model and
14: loses quality with no error, so the test suite pins the expected vector.
15: 
16: The artifact is dynamically quantized: the activation scale of a run comes from

## 2. Critical & High-Severity Findings

### 2.1. `LLMClient` and `JevClient` Refuse to Call Real Models in `development` Mode and Silently Swallow API Errors
- **Locations**:
  - [`LLMClient.complete`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/integrations/llm/client.py#L26-L98) (lines 34–36 and 86–87)
  - [`JevClient._call_llm`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/integrations/jev/jev.py#L36-L65) (lines 44–45 and 63–64)
  - [`deploy/docker-compose.yml`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/deploy/docker-compose.yml#L30-L60)
- **Issue**:
  1. In [`LLMClient.complete`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/integrations/llm/client.py#L34-L36):
     ```python
     api_key = self.settings.REASONING_LLM_API_KEY
     if not api_key or self.settings.APP_ENV in ("test", "development"):
         return self._fallback_complete(messages, selected_model)
     ```
     Because [`Settings.APP_ENV`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/config/settings.py#L14) defaults to `"development"` (including in [`deploy/docker-compose.yml`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/deploy/docker-compose.yml#L31)), **configuring `REASONING_LLM_API_KEY` in a standard local or Docker Compose deployment still bypasses the LLM entirely** and returns the stub `"Acknowledged: ..."` with zero tool calls. The same check exists in [`JevClient._call_llm`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/integrations/jev/jev.py#L44-L45).
  2. Even in `production`, lines 86–87 catch all exceptions and return the stub completion:
     ```python
     except Exception:
         return self._fallback_complete(messages, selected_model)
     ```
     Any provider HTTP `401`, `429`, `500`, or network timeout is converted into an assistant turn saying `"Acknowledged: <prompt>"` with `tool_calls=[]`, causing [`RunLoop`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py#L510-L518) to mark the run `completed` with a fake answer instead of failing/retrying the job.
- **Fix**: Only use `_fallback_complete` when `APP_ENV == "test"` (or when an explicit `LLM_MOCK_FALLBACK=True` flag is set), and allow `httpx.HTTPError` to propagate in non-test environments so the worker job retry policy handles transient LLM failures.

### 2.2. Context Compaction Is Never Wired Into `RunLoop` and Has an Interface/Persistence Mismatch
- **Locations**:
  - [`RunsService.build_loop`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/service.py#L90-L115)
  - [`CompactionProvider`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py#L139-L144) & [`RunLoop._compact_check`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py#L549-L558)
  - [`CompactionService.compact`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/compaction/service.py#L436-L474)
- **Issue**:
  1. [`RunsService.__init__`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/service.py#L72-L88) and [`RunsService.build_loop`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/service.py#L90-L115) never accept or pass `compactor=` to [`RunLoop`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py#L334). In production (`worker.py` / `dependencies.py`), `loop.compactor` is always `None`, so Stage 2 (`compact_check`) is a no-op once a run hits the 80% token watermark.
  2. Even if passed in, [`RunLoop._compact_check`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py#L554-L557) calls:
     ```python
     compacted = await self.compactor.compact(run.id, assembled.messages)
     if compacted:
         return await self.journal.list_messages(run.id), True
     ```
     Here `assembled.messages` is a `tuple[MessageDTO, ...]`, whereas [`CompactionService.compact`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/compaction/service.py#L436-L474) expects `Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]` (calling `message.get(...)` in [`tiers.py`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/compaction/tiers.py#L64), which raises `AttributeError` on [`MessageDTO`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/state.py#L134-L144)) and returns a [`CompactedContext`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/compaction/tiers.py#L52-L58) object rather than rewriting the `messages` table in [`SqlRunJournal`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/state.py#L653-L887). Re-reading `self.journal.list_messages(run.id)` on line 557 would therefore reload the uncompacted messages from PostgreSQL.
- **Fix**: Inject [`CompactionService`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/compaction/service.py#L338) into [`RunsService`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/service.py#L72), adapt [`MessageDTO`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/state.py#L134-L144) $\leftrightarrow$ mapping format (or have `RunLoop._compact_check` use the returned `CompactedContext.messages` directly), and persist the compacted checkpoint into the run’s journal.
